title: GoPIM: GCN-Oriented Pipeline Optimization for PIM Accelerators
problem: ReRAM-based PIM accelerators for GCN training suffer from severe pipeline underutilization due to skewed execution times across GCN stages (aggregation, combination) and skewed degree distributions of graph vertices, causing crossbar resource imbalance.
motivation: GCNs are widely used for graph learning but require frequent memory access; ReRAM PIM offers in-situ computing to address the memory bottleneck, yet naive pipelining fails to exploit the full potential due to stage and vertex heterogeneity.
method: GoPIM uses machine learning to watch which pipeline stages are lagging and dynamically shifts ReRAM crossbar resources (physical computing elements) to the stage that needs them most at any moment. It also uses interleaved vertex mapping to spread graph nodes across multiple crossbars so that nodes with more connections don't all end up on the same resource. Together, these reduce execution time while maintaining accuracy.
key_novelty: The innovation is a machine-learning policy that dynamically shifts ReRAM crossbar resources to pipeline stages based on real-time bottlenecks, combined with interleaved vertex mapping to distribute graph nodes despite their skewed degree distributions (many nodes have far more connections than others).
contributions: ML-based scheme for dynamic crossbar resource allocation to bottleneck GCN pipeline stages
Selective vertex updating technique with interleaved crossbar mapping to handle skewed vertex degrees
Practical GoPIM architecture design for ReRAM PIM
Up to 191x speedup and 16.1x energy saving vs. state-of-the-art work
primary_theme: pipeline-aware ReRAM PIM optimization for GCN training
